item.title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked pilot with axe in attempted 'terrorist attack', UAE says
item.description: Investigations are ongoing to determine the circumstances of the incident, the motives and any related connections, as well as to examine physical and digital evidence, the UAE's prosecutor general said.
item.dc:creator: Eman Abouhassira, Maha Dahan, Alexander Cornwell
item.content:encoded: The co-pilot of flydubai [USN:L1N45O0FU TEXT:"flight FZ1073"], which was bound for Israel, attempted to carry out a "terrorist attack" with an axe during the flight, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said on Saturday. The co-pilot was identified as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national, a source with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters. A second source briefed on the investigation confirmed the co-pilot’s name. UAE authorities did not immediately respond to a request for confirmation of his identity. Disaster was averted on Wednesday after passengers and crew [USN:L1N45M07P TEXT:"subdued the co-pilot"], who had attacked the captain in what Israeli officials said was an apparent attempt to crash the plane carrying more than 170 passengers and crew. While Emirati authorities and the airline have not publicly identified the co-pilot, Israeli officials have previously said he is an Omani national. Oman has not commented on the incident. "Investigations into the incident involving flydubai flight FZ1073 found that the co-pilot had attempted to carry out a terrorist attack," Prosecutor General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said in a statement carried by the UAE's state news agency. The co-pilot attacked the pilot inside the cockpit with a crash axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft, the prosecutor general said. A crash axe is typically kept in the cockpit for use during emergencies such as crashes. The investigation into flight FZ1073, including the suspect's motives, is ongoing, and the findings will be released once the "necessary procedures" have been completed, the prosecutor general said. The UAE is leading the investigation. The airline is owned by Dubai's government. MOST PASSENGERS ON FLIGHT WERE ISRAELI The prosecutor general's comments were the first by Emirati investigators to describe the incident as an attempted terrorist attack. Following the release of the prosecutor general's statement, Anwar Gargash, a senior adviser to the UAE president, said on X that the Gulf country had zero tolerance for terrorism and would show no leniency toward extremist rhetoric. Flydubai said the circumstances surrounding the incident were still under investigation and that it was not in a position to comment further, a spokesperson said on Saturday. Reuters could not immediately verify professional and social media pages reportedly belonging to the co-pilot, which suggested he had worked for other airlines. Royal Air Maroc told Reuters, in response to a question about his potential employment there in the past, that he had undergone a three-month training with the airline in 2025 but his application to work there afterwards was rejected. RAM did not elaborate. In his first public comments on the incident, flydubai Chief Executive Ghaith al Ghaith on Friday said that the flight diverted after a "safety incident" inside the cockpit. Most of the passengers on board were Israeli nationals. A reserve flydubai pilot travelling on the flight took control of the aircraft and landed it at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, where the co-pilot was detained by Saudi authorities. The co-pilot was transferred from Saudi Arabia to Abu Dhabi on Thursday. A source briefed on the investigation told Reuters on Friday that Israeli officials were [USN:L1N45O0GL TEXT:"expected to question"] the co-pilot in the UAE. The source declined to say which Israeli agency or authority would take part. An Israeli government official said that Israeli investigators would take part alongside Emirati authorities in the UAE-led investigation. Israel does not have official diplomatic relations with Oman, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said pilots from such countries were not permitted to operate flights to Israel. It was not clear how the co-pilot came to be assigned to the flight to Tel Aviv. On Friday, Netanyahu said that Israel was looking into whether the co-pilot had acted under anyone's direction, warning that anyone involved would pay a "heavy price". The aircraft dropped about 16,625 feet in just over 30 seconds while flying over Saudi Arabia on its journey from the UAE to Israel, according to flight-tracking data from Flightradar24. The route is popular among Israeli travellers.

item.title: 独経済、今年1％前後成長も 財政支出と輸出寄与と連銀総裁
item.description: ［フランクフルト ２日 ロイター］ - ドイツ連邦銀行（中央銀行）のナーゲル総裁は２日、同国の今年の成長率が１％前後...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
独経済、今年1％前後成長も　財政支出と輸出寄与と連銀総裁 15:46 配信

2023年11月、キプロス中央銀行で開催された会合で撮影　REUTERS/Yiannis Kourtoglou

［フランクフルト　２日　ロイター］ - ドイツ連邦銀行（中央銀行）のナーゲル総裁は２日、同国の今年の成長率が１％前後になる可能性があると述べた。堅調な輸出需要と政府投資が寄与する。同中銀が６月に示した予測（０．５％）の２倍となる。

ドイツは過去３年間ほとんど成長していない。イラン戦争に起因するエネルギー価格高騰が産業に打撃を与えている。

ナーゲル氏は講演で、生産は予想外に底堅いと指摘した。潜在成長率は依然として低いものの、ドイツは景気循環上の回復局面にあるとの認識を示した。

「年平均で１％前後の実質経済成長となる可能性は十分にある」と述べ、「３年間の停滞を経て、これは確かに小さいながらも歓迎すべき兆しとなるだろう」とした。

ナーゲル氏は、連邦政府の国防やインフラなどに重点を置いた財政支出を成長けん引役の一つとし、予想外に堅調な海外需要の恩恵も受けているとした。

ドイツの主要経済研究所も先月下旬に、今年と来年の経済成長率予測を上方修正した。今年の成長率予測は０．６％から１．３％に引き上げられた。

item.title: Marquez wins Japanese GP sprint to close in on Martin
item.description: Ducati's Marc Marquez won the Japanese Grand Prix sprint on Saturday to shave five points off Aprilia rider Jorge Martin's lead in the MotoGP championship standings.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ducati's Marc Marquez won the Japanese Grand Prix sprint on Saturday to shave five points off Aprilia rider Jorge Martin's lead in the MotoGP championship standings. Marquez made a scorching start and held the inside line on the first turn of the opening lap to surge past Martin, who had set a lap record at the Motegi circuit earlier on Saturday [USN:L4N45P00C TEXT:"to grab pole position"]. Reigning champion Marquez maintained his lead and coasted to victory, moving him to 306 points - seven behind Martin (313), ahead of Sunday's race. "The target was front row in the qualifying. Starting on first or second was the best place to do a great sprint race," seven-times world champion Marquez said. "We did a small modification for the sprint race, and I felt much better on the bike." Aprilia's Martin finished second, but was demoted to third behind LCR Honda's Diogo Moreira. The Spaniard had found it hard going towards the end of the sprint as he was put under pressure by Tech3's Enea Bastianini, with the thrilling duel leading both riders to stray outside the track. "I tried in the last lap to do everything I could to keep Enea behind. I achieved that," Martin said. "I don't know exactly where I touched (the outside), because I was really focused on not doing it. So, big mistake." Brazilian Moreira earned his first sprint podium. It was also the first sprint podium for satellite team LCR since 2023. "Today was the day. We saw the crash and I said, 'OK, today I will try to push to see'. At the end, lap by lap, I was feeling more comfortable with the bike," the 22-year-old said. KTM's Pedro Acosta, fresh off the [USN:L1N45C039 TEXT:"first MotoGP victory of his career"] , started in the front row but quickly found himself in the gravel after being involved in a three-rider crash along with Alex Marquez and Fabio Di Giannantonio. Japan's Ai Ogura (Trackhouse) finished fifth, ahead of Martin's Aprilia teammate Marco Bezzecchi, whose outside bid for the championship was dealt another blow.

item.title: NHL roundup: Alex Tuch, Caps send champ Hurricanes to 2nd straight loss
item.description: Alex Tuch scored two first-period goals in his first game with Washington, allowing the Capitals to coast to a season-opening 5-2 victory against the Carolina Hurricanes on Friday in Raleigh, N.C.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Alex Tuch scored two first-period goals in his first game with Washington, allowing the Capitals to coast to a season-opening 5-2 victory against the Carolina Hurricanes on Friday in Raleigh, N.C. Jakob Chychrun had a goal and an assist while Cole Hutson and Ryan Leonard also scored for the Capitals, who opened their schedule three nights after some other teams in the NHL. Dylan Strome and Pierre-Luc Dubois each had two assists for Washington while Alex Ovechkin, beginning his 22nd season, added an assist. Capitals goalie Logan Thompson stopped 31 shots. Sebastian Aho and Logan Stankoven scored for Carolina, which needed nearly 102 minutes of game time to put the puck in the net at the outset of its Stanley Cup title defense. Hurricanes goalie Brandon Bussi, playing for the second time this week, made 22 saves. Bruins 4, Jets 3 (OT) JJ Peterka scored with 1:39 left in overtime, propelling Boston to a come-from-behind win at Winnipeg. The Bruins' Elias Lindholm scored an extra-attacker goal with 1:38 left in regulation to force OT. Hampus Lindholm and James Hagens (first NHL goal) also tallied while Jeremy Swayman made 30 saves for Boston, which has started the season with back-to-back wins. David Pastrnak assisted on Boston's last two goals. Kyle Connor had a power-play goal and added an assist, Mario Ferraro and Dylan DeMelo also lit the lamp, and Adam Lowry dished out a pair of helpers for the Jets in their season opener. Stuart Skinner turned aside 26 shots. Rangers 2, Red Wings 0 Dylan Garand posted his first career shutout while making 22 saves as New York blanked host Detroit. Sean Durzi scored on a first-period power play and Eeli Tolvanen chipped in an empty-net goal to spoil the Red Wings' season opener. Garand was making his first start this season after going 2-0-1 in three appearances for the Rangers last season. John Gibson made 19 saves for the Red Wings, who were missing two of their top players. Former captain and first-line center Dylan Larkin, who has requested a trade, was sidelined by an upper-body injury, while restricted free agent Simon Edvinsson, one of the team's top defensemen, remains unsigned amid stalled negotiations. Blues 4, Stars 0 Joel Hofer made 25 saves for his ninth career shutout and contributed an assist as visiting St. Louis beat Dallas in the season opener for both teams. Pius Suter and Jimmy Snuggerud each had a goal and an assist and Mason McTavish and Dalibor Dvorsky also scored for the Blues. McTavish recorded his goal 1:34 into his St. Louis debut after he was acquired in an offseason trade with Anaheim. Stars goalie Jake Oettinger stopped 20 shots, but Dallas was unable to find the net despite holding a 25-24 edge in shots on goal. The Blues led just 2-0 before tacking on a pair of empty-net goals in a 15-second span over the final 2:30. Ducks 4, Golden Knights 3 Leo Carlsson had a goal and an assist and Lukas Dostal made 27 saves as Anaheim jumped out to a four-goal lead and held on for a victory in Las Vegas. Beckett Sennecke, Alex Killorn and Jeff Malott also tallied for the Ducks in their season opener. Shea Theodore, Tomas Hertl and Braeden Bowman scored goals and Jack Eichel had two assists for the Golden Knights, who fell to 15-4-1 in regular-season home games against Anaheim. Carter Hart finished with 16 saves. --Field Level Media

item.title: Antonelli finds his rhythm to top final Sepang practice
item.description: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli topped the final practice session for the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Saturday after the Mercedes driver finally found his rhythm at the Sepang International Circuit.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli topped the final practice session for the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Saturday after the Mercedes driver finally found his rhythm at the Sepang International Circuit. The 20-year-old was only eighth fastest in [USN:L1N45O07M TEXT:"Friday's FP2 "]but improved to clock 1 minute 36.302 seconds on soft tyres. Red Bull's four-times champion Max Verstappen, the last driver to win at Sepang in 2017, was second fastest, while his team mate Isack Hadjar was third, a little over half a second slower than Antonelli. Mercedes driver George Russell, who trails his teammate by 66 points in the standings, was fourth fastest, over six-tenths of a second slower, but ahead of the two Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton. "It felt like a pretty decent lap considering the tyres were not great," Hamilton said over the team radio. McLaren's reigning world champion Lando Norris, the only driver in the top 10 on medium tyres, was seventh fastest followed by his team mate Oscar Piastri. Alpine's Franco Colapinto and Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad completed the top 10. The session was briefly red-flagged midway through to remove debris from the circuit after it got tangled in Haas driver Oliver Bearman's front-right tyre, with the Briton asking his team on the radio if they knew what it was. Malaysia is hosting the Bahrain race due to the conflict in the Middle East.

item.title: Indonesia detects new land formations from Anak Krakatau eruptions
item.description: Indonesia's Anak Krakatau volcano expanded by 32.8 hectares (81 acres) after eruptions produced lava flows, while satellite imagery detected two new land formations nearby, the country's Geology Agency said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indonesia's Anak Krakatau volcano expanded by 32.8 hectares (81 acres) after eruptions produced lava flows, while satellite imagery detected two new land formations nearby, the country's Geology Agency said. The increase was identified by comparing Sentinel satellite images from August 8 and September 15, the agency posted on social media in late September Anak Krakatau erupted for 25 hours from September 4 to September 6, sending lava towards the northwest, west and southwest. Sentinel imagery from September 23 showed a new formation about 760 metres (2,500 feet) northwest of Anak Krakatau's coastline and another about 495 metres (1,620 feet) southeast The two formations, on either side of the volcano's crater, may be linked to the eruptions, the agency said. More recent data and further analysis are needed to determine whether they were new eruption centres, it said Mount Anak Krakatau's eruptions sent ash over Jakarta and surrounding areas, caused several [USN:L1N44Y005 TEXT:"airports to be closed,"] affecting more than 340,000 travellers, with 2,961 flights cancelled, delayed or diverted Anak Krakatau is one of about 130 active volcanoes in Indonesia, which straddles the "Pacific Ring of Fire", a highly seismically active zone where different plates on the earth's crust meet to create a large number of earthquakes and volcanic eruptions. Anak Krakatau, which means child of Krakatau, began emerging a century ago from the area previously occupied by Krakatau, then known as Krakatoa. The older volcano destroyed itself in mass eruptions in 1883, which killed more than 36,000 people after triggering a series of tsunamis.

item.title: トランプ氏、公的医療保険加入者に90ドル給付表明 2000万人超
item.description:
Kanishka Singh
［ワシントン ２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Kanishka Singh

［ワシントン　２日　ロイター］ - トランプ米大統領は、高齢者向け公的医療保険「メディケア」に加入する米国民２０００万人超に対し、毎月の保険料負担を軽減するため、１人当たり９０ドルを一時金として支給すると表明した。

トランプ氏は２日深夜、自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）への投稿で、給付金は「メディケア改善基金」から拠出すると説明。同基金には、メディケアの出来高払い制度の改善を目的として議会から２０億ドルが拠出されているとした。

ホワイトハウスのウェブサイトによると、対象の高齢者の大半に１０月上旬に９０ドルが銀行口座に直接振り込まれる。口座振り込みを利用していない対象者には、メディケアに登録した住所に小切手を送付する。発送も１０月上旬になるという。

トランプ氏は１１月の中間選挙を前に、有権者にばらまき的施策を打ち出している。９月には、中間選挙で勝利すれば成人に５０００ドルの「トランプ配当」を給付すると提案した。

政権は、１００万人近い米国民への５００ドルの給付も進めている。ホワイトハウスは、この５００ドルの給付について、医療保険制度改革法（ＡＣＡ）に基づく保険の加入者から過剰に徴収されたとする保険料の払い戻しだと説明している。給付は全米を対象としたものでなく、連邦政府の医療保険加入サイトを利用する３０州の一部住民に限られる。対象州には主要な激戦州が多く含まれ、選挙戦略の専門家らは、一部の選挙戦の結果に影響を及ぼす可能性があると指摘している。

item.title: US Debt Path Leaves It ‘Increasingly Exposed,’ Scope Warns

item.title: Japan's penalty hero wants more home fans to embrace women's game
item.description: Japan's penalty hero Yuzuho Shiokoshi hopes her team's soccer gold medal on home soil can get more local fans to embrace the women's game after a modest crowd attended their Asian Games shootout win over North Korea.
item.dc:creator: Ian Ransom
item.content:encoded: Japan's penalty hero Yuzuho Shiokoshi hopes her team's soccer gold medal on home soil can get more local fans to embrace the women's game after a modest crowd attended their Asian Games shootout win over North Korea. Some 6,000 people watched [USN:L6N45O0LF TEXT:"Friday's final"] at the 50,000-seat Shizuoka Stadium, while the host broadcaster opted to cover the men's volleyball semi-final between Japan and China instead. A day earlier, 65,000 spectators watched the Japanese men's national team beat Ecuador on penalties in the Kirin Cup in Yokohama. Japan's women claimed their third successive Asian Games gold, three years after beating North Korea in front of 37,000 fans in Hangzhou, China. "The crowd today might have been large for this tournament, but compared to last time in Hangzhou, I feel like we're still not quite there," said Shiokoshi, who struck the winning penalty on Friday. "We're out there fighting hard, and we want people to come and see us play in person. "It's tough at times, given that women's football isn't always prioritised for TV broadcasts." Japan selected a squad made up almost exclusively of home-based players rather than their top players in Europe despite the Games' tournament falling largely within the September-October international window. Shiokoshi, a midfielder for Tokyo Verdy Beleza in Japan's WE League, said her teammates' performances had been a good advertisement for the women's top flight. "I hope this encourages more people to come and watch WE League matches, and that it helps generate some excitement around the league," she said. “I think winning the title can boost the league’s value."

item.title: Bridge across Dnipro river in Kyiv hit during Russian attack, mayor says
item.description: The Northern Bridge across the Dnipro river in Kyiv was hit during a Russian air attack on Saturday, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, amid an escalation in strikes on infrastructure in the Ukrainian capital.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Northern Bridge across the Dnipro river in Kyiv was hit during a Russian air attack on Saturday, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, amid an escalation in strikes on infrastructure in the Ukrainian capital. Emergency services were deployed to the scene, the mayor said, and traffic across the bridge from the east to the west bank was suspended following damage to the road surface and the overhead trolleybus cables. There were no casualties reported. In the past two days, the Southern Bridge has been struck several times by Russian drones, forcing the temporary suspension of traffic across it and two other bridges across the vast Dnipro river. Over a third of the capital's 3 million residents lived on the east, or "left", bank of the Dnipro before Russia's 2022 invasion, but the vast majority work on the western, or "right", bank where most government institutions and companies are. Memories of last winter, the worst of the war, are prominent in residents' minds after Russia launched last week what was seen in Ukraine as the first salvo of an expected winter bombing campaign against power facilities supplying the capital. Moscow has previously denied systematically targeting civilians as part of its bombing campaigns.

item.title: Swarms of moths in Australia lift hopes of recovery for endangered species
item.description: Swarms of moths blanketing homes in Australia's southeast in recent days signalled the endangered species is recovering, authorities said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Swarms of moths blanketing homes in Australia's southeast in recent days signalled the endangered species is recovering, authorities said on Saturday. Bogong moths, with a wingspan of up to 5 cm (2 inches), have experienced years of steep population decline, decreasing the visibility of their southern spring migration to caves in the Australian Alps in a journey that can be up to 3,000 km (1,900 miles). But the moths have had a comeback this year, with reports that the insects have invaded backyards and homes along Australia's east coast, including in New South Wales state capital, Sydney. "It’s really exciting to see this recovering population coming our way," Steve Whan, who represents the alpine area of Monaro in the New South Wales parliament, said in a statement. "The Bogongs are terrific for our ecosystem, supporting our treasured native wildlife like the pygmy-possum and pollinating our eucalyptus trees." In neighbouring Victoria state, Chief Biodiversity Officer James Todd said it was exciting to see the moths returning in large numbers this year. "The jump in numbers is a positive sign for biodiversity," Todd said in a statement. The numbers of the moths, which are harmless to humans and legally protected, have fallen due to drought, agricultural intensification and habitat loss, authorities say. One theory for the rebound is more rainfall in northern New South Wales producing extra food for the insects' larvae, the Australian Broadcasting Corp reported.

Yamal and Mbappé don’t deserve the Ballon d’Or

Lamine Yamal has a World Cup. Kylian Mbappé has 58 goals. Neither has done enough to bag the Ballon d’Or.

Mohammad Hammad

03 October, 2026 10:52 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Kylian Mbappe (L) and Lamine Yamal are the favourites of this year to win the Ballon d'Or | Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

F or almost 15 years, Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo made the Ballon d’Or—football’s most prestigious individual award—their own private battleground. The duo dominated the game, scored goals, broke records and won almost every major title there was. Most importantly, they did their talking on the pitch .

This year, the battle feels different.

After the fierce competition between two all-time greats, we now have a “beg-to-beg” competition between French striker Kylian Mbappe and Spanish winger Lamine Yamal. B oth are self-advocating their brilliance in the media, claiming they have done enough to win the award.

Show Full Article

Their individual brilliance is undeniable, and the numbers speak for themselves. But when those individual achievements are measured against their teams’ actual success, the tall claims become a little harder to swallow.

Have they actually done enough to deserve the Ballon d’Or?

Weak case for Yamal and Mbappe Yamal’s Ballon d’Or claim is heavily built around Spain’s World Cup triumph, but his individual numbers at the tournament leave a lot to be desired. He finished the World Cup with just one goal and one assist. Of course, context matters. Yamal entered the tournament after recovering from an injury and following an exhausting season with Barcelona, where he was a key figure in their domestic success, scoring 16 goals and providing 12 assists.

While he was the player of the season in La Liga, Barcelona’s biggest ambition — winning the Champions League — remained an unfulfilled dream since 2015. They were knocked out in the quarter-finals by Diego Simeone’s Atlético Madrid. So, when we look at Yamal’s entire season rather than just the World Cup and Spain’s success, does his resume truly make him the standout player of the year? No, it doesn’t.

Then there is Mbappé, whose case is almost entirely built around his numbers. And this is where the debate becomes particularly interesting.

Mbappé finished as the top scorer across all major competitions with 58 goals for club and country: 25 in La Liga, 15 in the Champions League and 10 for France at the World Cup.

On paper, those numbers are extraordinary. But let’s put these numbers into perspective.

Mbappé scored 25 goals in La Liga, but only 17 came from open play — fewer than Vedat Muriqi of Mallorca, whose side was relegated last season. In the Champions League, Mbappé won the Golden Boot with 15 goals, but 13 of those came during the initial league phase, against opponents such as Benfica, Marseille, Kairat, Monaco and Olympiacos.

His World Cup campaign, however, is much harder to question. He won the Golden Boot after scoring 10 goals. But even that achievement came with a caveat: his final goal tally was boosted by his hat-trick in the third-place play-off against England, a match English forward Harry Kane did not play.

And then there is the bigger picture: Mbappé ended another season without a major trophy.

That makes his own claim particularly fascinating. Mbappé has said: “For years, I’ve considered myself the best player in the world. I haven’t seen anyone better than me.” He also said he would accept Messi or Ronaldo winning the Ballon d’Or, but he would not have swapped places with anyone else who has won it.

But would the recent winners have wanted to swap places with him?

Would Luka Modrić, who led Croatia to a historic World Cup F inal in 2018 , have traded his Ballon d’Or for Mbappé’s goals? Would Karim Benzema, Rodri or Ousmane Dembélé? Would they have exchanged their trophies, titles and defining moments for individual numbers?

That, for me, is where the Ballon d’Or debate becomes more complicated.

Also read: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal exit is another selfish tantrum. He is ruining his legacy

Goals alone won’t suffice Individual numbers matter, goals matter. But football is ultimately a team sport, and individual brilliance becomes far more significant when it is backed by collective success — unless the numbers are so extraordinary that they become impossible to ignore, like Messi’s 91 goals in 2012.

This isn’t an argument against Mbappé. His numbers are remarkable, and his World Cup campaign was exceptional. But after almost a decade at the very top of football, his defining achievement remains the 2018 World Cup.

Let’s remember Mbappe plays for two of the biggest teams in Real Madrid and France, where numbers should also translate into the team’s achievements.

Because if goals alone are supposed to be the strongest argument for the Ballon d’Or, then why isn’t Harry Kane making the same case?

Kane has scored 73 goals across all competitions this season — 15 more than Mbappe.

Meanwhile, m any are backing Messi to win it for the record ninth time after a magical World Cup run from the little maestro at the age of 39. Messi scored eight goals and provided four assists—two of which came against England in the semi-finals. At 39, Messi once again showed why he’s still in contention for the golden ball.

Although the award is slowly losing its credibility, and with this being the World Cup year, the winner will surely be scrutinised. The debate and claims are only going to catch fire as there are no clear favourites this time. But the self-advocacy outburst of Mbappe and Yamal is surely a bit too far from what they managed to achieve. While Yamal’s Spain and Barcelona bested Mbappe’s France and Real Madrid, this doesn’t mean that he was the point of difference every time the two met on the field.

While Harry Kane also failed to secure anything big with his team and Messi is not playing in Europe, it’ll be interesting to see who takes home the award on 26 October.

(Edited by Saptak Datta)

item.title: Canucks eager to fix defensive problems as Flames visit
item.description: The Vancouver Canucks will try to shore up a leaky defense when they host the Calgary Flames on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Vancouver Canucks will try to shore up a leaky defense when they host the Calgary Flames on Saturday. Vancouver finished with the lowest point total in the NHL last season (58) while permitting a league-leading 314 goals. The early returns on the new season show no improvement in the latter area. The Canucks surrendered 14 goals in a home-and-home series against the Oilers. Vancouver won the season opener 6-5 in overtime at Edmonton. Two nights later in Vancouver, the Oilers jumped out to a 5-0 lead early in the second period and then held on for a 9-7 victory. "That wasn't anywhere near close to good enough," said Canucks defenseman Luke Schenn, one of the veterans the team brought in during the offseason to bring leadership to the dressing room. "(The Oilers) got a couple of guys that are elite players. You give them a ton of respect and they are going to burn you." Schenn warned his teammates against getting selfish with the puck. "You get on your own program at times," he said. "You become an individual and turn the puck over, get sloppy and hang your goalie out to dry on breakaways. The good news on both sides is we don't have to see (Edmonton) for awhile." First-year coach Manny Malhotra wasn't happy with the way Vancouver fell behind 8-2 halfway through the Thursday game after giving up short-handed goals to Connor McDavid and Kasperi Kapanen 34 seconds apart on the same penalty kill. "We didn't seem to be as prepared as we needed to be," Malhotra said. "That is how the game got away from us. We lost the majority of puck battles and the majority of races. They were more hungrier." The Canucks are firmly in rebuild mode. Last season was a dismal campaign for Vancouver, punctuated by a franchise-record 11-game losing streak (0-9-2) and the departure of captain Quinn Hughes, who soured on playing in Vancouver and was traded to the Minnesota Wild in December. Vancouver is still without a captain. Instead of giving the "C" to someone else, the Canucks decided to appoint six alternate captains. The Flames are also trying to get over a poor 2025-26 season, when they tied for the NHL's third-lowest point total (77). The biggest problem was an offense that produced a league-low 208 goals. Calgary was hammered 6-1 in its season opener by the visiting Seattle Kraken on Thursday, the Flames' largest margin of defeat ever in a home opener. Ryan Strome scored for the Flames. Goalie Dustin Wolf stopped 26 shots against Seattle in what is expected to be the final season opener at the Saddledome. "You saw all our warts in one night," coach Ryan Huska said. Like the Canucks, the Flames fell behind early and gave up five consecutive goals to start the game. Calgary was outshot 32-25 and had just one power play while conceding five. "That one stings," Strome said. "It is disappointing. We are a team that can't make any mistakes. We got to play hard and we got to play simple. Getting away from that was what you saw tonight." --Field Level Media

item.title: Sharks push for more early-season success against Kings
item.description: The San Jose Sharks will look to show more of their identity when they face the visiting Los Angeles Kings on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The San Jose Sharks will look to show more of their identity when they face the visiting Los Angeles Kings on Saturday. San Jose opened the season with a 4-3 overtime win over the Florida Panthers on Thursday. Will Smith scored two goals and added an assist, and Mason Marchment also tallied in his Sharks debut as San Jose opened a 3-0 lead. Luca Cagnoni added his first career goal in the extra period after the Sharks squandered the lead in regulation. Macklin Celebrini contributed three assists and Yaroslav Askarov made 23 saves in the win. "There was a lot going on in that game, a lot that we can kind of build off of and learn from," Sharks coach Ryan Warsofsky said. "We said it before the game: It wasn't going to be perfect, we weren't going to be perfect. But we wanted to show our identity, and I thought we did that more often (on Thursday) than we probably have in the last couple years." Saturday is the first of four meetings between the Pacific Division rivals. San Jose won two of three matchups with the Kings last season. Askarov, the Sharks' expected starter, is 3-1-0 with a 2.94 goals-against average and an .878 save percentage in four career appearances against the Kings. Following the Saturday contest, the Sharks head on the road for a pair of Central Division matchups against the Dallas Stars on Monday and the St. Louis Blues on Thursday. "We want to play fast, we want to get on teams with our team speed, but we need to be physical, and that's what winning teams do. They're physical all over the ice," Warsofsky said. "That doesn't mean you're running around trying to put people into Section 220 in the stands. It's just playing through people and being hard to play against." The Kings travel to San Jose cap a two-game, season-opening road trip after being doubled up 8-4 by the Colorado Avalanche in Denver on Wednesday. Brian Dumoulin, Joel Armia, Trevor Moore and Artemi Panarin scored for the Kings. Alex Laferriere added two assists in Los Angeles' first regular-season game under new coach Peter Laviolette. Darcy Kuemper made 21 saves in the loss. "I think that there were things that we did well and I think that there are things that we need to clean up and do better," Laviolette said. "I felt like a lot of the things that we gave (Colorado) were our responsibility. They are things that can be in our control: staying out of the penalty box, the execution of what we're doing, staying behind the rush. We got chances to score offensively, and we didn't connect on them. "So we found ourselves chasing the game most of the night." In 22 career games against the Sharks, Kuemper is 10-5-5 with a .909 save percentage and a 2.78 GAA. The Kings head back to Los Angeles following the Saturday game for their home opener against the Panthers on Tuesday. --Field Level Media

item.title: Leo Carlsson, Ducks start strong, hold off Golden Knights’ surge
item.description: Leo Carlsson had a goal and an assist and Lukas Dostal made 27 saves as the Anaheim Ducks jumped out to a big early lead and held on for a 4-3 victory over the Vegas Golden Knights on Friday night in Las Vegas.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Leo Carlsson had a goal and an assist and Lukas Dostal made 27 saves as the Anaheim Ducks jumped out to a big early lead and held on for a 4-3 victory over the Vegas Golden Knights on Friday night in Las Vegas. Beckett Sennecke, Alex Killorn and Jeff Malott also scored goals for Anaheim in its season-opener. Shea Theodore, Tomas Hertl and Braeden Bowman scored goals and Jack Eichel had two assists for Vegas, which lost in regulation for just the fourth time (15-4-1) in 20 regular-season games against Anaheim at T-Mobile Arena. Carter Hart finished with 16 saves for the Golden Knights. Anaheim took a 1-0 lead at the 19:52 mark of the first period on a breakaway goal by Sennecke. Carlsson picked up the primary assist on the play with a highlight-reel stretch pass from deep in his own zone to Sennecke, who snuck behind a pair of Vegas defenders and then beat Hart with a wrist shot on his glove side. The Ducks extended the lead to 4-0 in the second period, scoring twice in the span of 55 seconds early in the period. Killorn, stationed in the slot, made it 2-0 at the 1:33 mark when he redirected Noah Warren's wrist shot from the right point over Hart's right shoulder. Warren, making his NHL debut, picked up an assist for his first career point. Malott followed with a goal on a double deflection. Jackson LaCombe fired a shot from the left point that Tim Washe deflected off Malott's skate and under Hart's pads. A wide-open Carlsson made it a four-goal lead at the 7:03 mark when he slammed in a rebound in the slot after Hart had turned away shots by Cutter Gauthier and A.J. Greer. Theodore cut the lead to 4-1 early in the third period when he snapped a wrist shot from the middle of the right circle over Dostal's left shoulder. Anaheim unsuccessfully challenged that Brett Howden was offside earlier in the play, earning the Ducks a two-minute delay of game penalty when the goal stood. Hertl then scored on the ensuing power play with a wrist shot in the slot off a Mitch Marner pass. Bowman then cut the deficit to one goal when he put in a rebound of a Victor Olofsson shot with 2:50 to go to make it 4-3. Vegas pulled Hart for an extra attacker with 2:15 left but Dostal turned away three shots in that final stretch. --Field Level Media

item.title: ゴルフ＝畑岡と山下が7位、首位と3打差 ロッテ選手権
item.description: ［２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２日　ロイター］ - 米女子ゴルフのロッテ選手権は２日、米ハワイ州エワビーチのホアカレイＣＣ（パー７２）で第２ラウンドを行い、前日３６位の畑岡奈紗が７バーディー、ノーボギーの６５をマークし、通算９アンダーの１３５で７位に浮上した。

１０位で出た山下美夢有も８バーディー、３ボギーの６７で回り、通算９アンダーで畑岡と並ぶ７位。首位とは３打差につけた。

岩井明愛は６９で回り、通算７アンダーの１３７で１４位。西郷真央は７０で通算６アンダーの１３８とし、２２位に後退した。

岩井千怜、竹田麗央、笹生優花は３３位。吉田優利は４５位、櫻井心那と西村優菜は５７位で、そのほかの日本選手は予選落ちとなった。

上位では、ポリー・マック（ドイツ）とジーノ・ティティクル（タイ）がともに６５をマークし、通算１２アンダーの１３２で首位。１打差の１１アンダーにカロリナ・メルグラティ（イタリア）とユン・イナ（韓国）が続いた。

item.title: AI's race to transform the world before the money runs out
item.description: Never has so much cash flowed into a new technology as is pouring into AI, eclipsing the sums splurged on railways or the internet when those technological revolutions sucked in capital.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Eisenhammer
item.content:encoded: Never has so much cash flowed into a new technology as is pouring into AI, eclipsing the sums splurged on railways or the internet when those technological revolutions sucked in capital. Cumulative spending globally on data centers alone could top $30 trillion by 2050, according to a projection by PwC, almost matching the [USN:S0N43F052 TEXT:"value of outstanding US Treasuries"]. It "dwarfs" what was spent in the railroad or dotcom booms, even after adjusting for inflation, PwC said. Meanwhile, Anthropic, just one of the major firms in the AI race, plans to spend $518 billion in coming years, according to the [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"IPO prospectus seen by Reuters"], which is more than 100 times its 2025 revenue. Its backers say AI technology will be more transformational than the advent of steam engines and the industrialization they powered. Yet lurking behind the dizzying projections and huge outlays by AI companies, alongside sky-high valuations, lie assumptions about vast broad-based productivity gains and future profits with little evidence so far - or historical precedent - to be sure they can deliver, economists say. PRODUCTIVITY GAINS 'REMAIN ELUSIVE' JP Morgan wrote in August that broad-based productivity gains in the US, which leads the AI race, "remain elusive", raising questions about the sustainability of AI valuations. A Bain & Company study said productivity gains from existing markets would not be enough to justify current outlays and "entirely new markets must emerge to close the funding gap", suggesting those could range from using AI-guided robots to developing new materials for batteries and semiconductors. US hyperscalers - the companies rolling out infrastructure around the world like Google, Amazon and Microsoft - and others in the AI race needed to find more than $4.2 trillion of new revenue in the next five years to fund the buildout, Bain said. "The question is whether the applications arrive in time to pay for it," according to the study, published last month. Few doubt the potential of AI to transform everything from work in an office to research labs, just as past revolutions shrank journey times from days to hours or connected the world at the touch of a keyboard. What seems more immutable is the maths behind securing a return on investment or the deadlines for repaying loans, leaving economists to work out the implications for the global economy beyond the ups and downs of investment cycles. "Historical precedent suggests that technology-driven booms often end when infrastructure buildouts cease to deliver sufficient returns," JP Morgan wrote. Using the example of Nvidia, the US company [USN:L1N45L0J4 TEXT:"whose chips are the backbone"] of the AI revolution, JP Morgan estimated US productivity gains would need to be 3% to 5% annually over the next 10 years to justify its valuation. That would be a substantial increase from the baseline expectation of the US Congressional Budget Office of 1.75% annual productivity growth for that period. For the US alone - which according to some estimates accounts for about three quarters of the global AI investment total - investment will run as high as about $9 trillion from 2025 to 2032, equivalent to spending 3.2% of US GDP each year, according to Columbia Business School economist Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh. He estimates the US AI sector would need to generate about $3.55 trillion in annual revenue by 2032 to earn a 10% return on investment. It earns a fraction of that now. The leveraged structure of much of the debt funding AI infrastructure also means "a relatively modest deterioration in demand, delays, or asset values can therefore produce much larger losses," he wrote in a conference paper, revised in October. AI AND 'THE RATE OF NEW WONDERS' The dizzying numbers have not stopped US AI bosses speaking with an otherworldly zeal about changes afoot. Anthropic's Dario Amodei has said an AI future could be "a thing of transcendent beauty", while OpenAI's Sam Altman has said "the rate of new wonders being achieved will be immense" as models learn to improve themselves and accelerate breakthroughs. Jasjeet Sekhon, chief strategy officer at Google DeepMind, told a summit at UC Berkeley in August that this self-teaching, known as recursive self-improvement, was a "key part of the investment thesis", and that it could, if achieved, deliver unprecedented productivity gains. Recursive self-improvement, while potentially delivering exponential AI advances, has also raised concerns about [USN:L4N45K1J5 TEXT:"existential risks"] to humanity. Yet the pace of change in productivity might still end up lagging the timelines needed by corporate accounts departments. Diane Coyle, an economist at Britain's Cambridge University, said the productivity impact of past revolutionary technologies had usually taken about 10 to 50 years to feed through. Anthropic's economics team modeled a range of scenarios for how much extra growth AI would deliver at an annual rate in 2030. Assuming a baseline of 2% in a non-AI environment, it suggested growth of 2.4% in a scenario with modest AI impact, 5.4% in a substantial scenario and 15.4% in an extreme scenario. Higher growth would mean more jobs lost, it said, without assigning probabilities for any of the outcomes. Amodei forecast last year that AI could wipe out half of all entry-level white-collar jobs within five years. For now, however, some researchers say it appears to have been limited to making it harder for those seeking office work to find a job. Studies in the US and Britain have pointed to a slowdown in early career hiring for white-collar positions performing tasks at which AI is adept, even if overall employment remains strong. Researchers at Stanford University said in August that employment of workers aged 22 to 25 in AI-exposed industries, such as accountants and paralegals, was 19% lower than for jobs that AI found hard to replicate, like janitors and builders. Yet even if the promised transformation takes longer than numbers surrounding AI companies imply, real economic benefits should stay - just as trains still ran after the Panic of 1873 that bankrupted railroad barons, while the internet didn't shut down after the 1990s dotcom bubble burst. "History is our friend in trying to understand this," said Coyle. "As long as one is left with the infrastructure that's needed to support all the productivity effects down the road, that's okay."

FAST

LONDON, Oct 3 : Never has so much cash flowed into a new technology as is pouring into AI, eclipsing the sums splurged on railways or the internet when those technological revolutions sucked in capital. Cumulative spending globally on data centers alone could top $30 trillion by 2050, according to a projection by PwC, almost matching the value of outstanding US Treasuries. It "dwarfs" what was spent in the railroad or dotcom booms, even after adjusting for inflation, PwC said. Meanwhile, Anthropic, just one of the major firms in the AI race, plans to spend $518 billion in coming years, according to the IPO prospectus seen by Reuters, which is more than 100 times its 2025 revenue. Its backers say AI technology will be more transformational than the advent of steam engines and the industrialization they powered. Yet lurking behind the dizzying projections and huge outlays by AI companies, alongside sky-high valuations, lie assumptions about vast broad-based productivity gains and future profits with little evidence so far - or historical precedent - to be sure they can deliver, economists say.

PRODUCTIVITY GAINS 'REMAIN ELUSIVE' JP Morgan wrote in August that broad-based productivity gains in the US, which leads the AI race, "remain elusive", raising questions about the sustainability of AI valuations. A Bain & Company study said productivity gains from existing markets would not be enough to justify current outlays and "entirely new markets must emerge to close the funding gap", suggesting those could range from using AI-guided robots to developing new materials for batteries and semiconductors. US hyperscalers - the companies rolling out infrastructure around the world like Google, Amazon and Microsoft - and others in the AI race needed to find more than $4.2 trillion of new revenue in the next five years to fund the buildout, Bain said. "The question is whether the applications arrive in time to pay for it," according to the study, published last month. Few doubt the potential of AI to transform everything from work in an office to research labs, just as past revolutions shrank journey times from days to hours or connected the world at the touch of a keyboard. What seems more immutable is the maths behind securing a return on investment or the deadlines for repaying loans, leaving economists to work out the implications for the global economy beyond the ups and downs of investment cycles. "Historical precedent suggests that technology-driven booms often end when infrastructure buildouts cease to deliver sufficient returns," JP Morgan wrote. Using the example of Nvidia, the US company whose chips are the backbone of the AI revolution, JP Morgan estimated US productivity gains would need to be 3 per cent to 5 per cent annually over the next 10 years to justify its valuation. That would be a substantial increase from the baseline expectation of the US Congressional Budget Office of 1.75 per cent annual productivity growth for that period. For the US alone - which according to some estimates accounts for about three quarters of the global AI investment total - investment will run as high as about $9 trillion from 2025 to 2032, equivalent to spending 3.2 per cent of US GDP each year, according to Columbia Business School economist Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh. He estimates the US AI sector would need to generate about $3.55 trillion in annual revenue by 2032 to earn a 10 per cent return on investment. It earns a fraction of that now. The leveraged structure of much of the debt funding AI infrastructure also means "a relatively modest deterioration in demand, delays, or asset values can therefore produce much larger losses," he wrote in a conference paper, revised in October. AI AND 'THE RATE OF NEW WONDERS' The dizzying numbers have not stopped US AI bosses speaking with an otherworldly zeal about changes afoot. Anthropic's Dario Amodei has said an AI future could be "a thing of transcendent beauty", while OpenAI's Sam Altman has said "the rate of new wonders being achieved will be immense" as models learn to improve themselves and accelerate breakthroughs. Jasjeet Sekhon, chief strategy officer at Google DeepMind, told a summit at UC Berkeley in August that this self-teaching, known as recursive self-improvement, was a "key part of the investment thesis", and that it could, if achieved, deliver unprecedented productivity gains. Recursive self-improvement, while potentially delivering exponential AI advances, has also raised concerns about existential risks to humanity. Yet the pace of change in productivity might still end up lagging the timelines needed by corporate accounts departments. Diane Coyle, an economist at Britain's Cambridge University, said the productivity impact of past revolutionary technologies had usually taken about 10 to 50 years to feed through. Anthropic's economics team modeled a range of scenarios for how much extra growth AI would deliver at an annual rate in 2030. Assuming a baseline of 2 per cent in a non-AI environment, it suggested growth of 2.4 per cent in a scenario with modest AI impact, 5.4 per cent in a substantial scenario and 15.4 per cent in an extreme scenario. Higher growth would mean more jobs lost, it said, without assigning probabilities for any of the outcomes. Amodei forecast last year that AI could wipe out half of all entry-level white-collar jobs within five years. For now, however, some researchers say it appears to have been limited to making it harder for those seeking office work to find a job. Studies in the US and Britain have pointed to a slowdown in early career hiring for white-collar positions performing tasks at which AI is adept, even if overall employment remains strong. Researchers at Stanford University said in August that employment of workers aged 22 to 25 in AI-exposed industries, such as accountants and paralegals, was 19 per cent lower than for jobs that AI found hard to replicate, like janitors and builders. Yet even if the promised transformation takes longer than numbers surrounding AI companies imply, real economic benefits should stay - just as trains still ran after the Panic of 1873 that bankrupted railroad barons, while the internet didn't shut down after the 1990s dotcom bubble burst. "History is our friend in trying to understand this," said Coyle. "As long as one is left with the infrastructure that's needed to support all the productivity effects down the road, that's okay."

Source: Reuters

item.title: When your journalism goes to Hollywood | On Assignment
item.description: Reporter Jeff Horwitz reflects on his Hollywood alter ego, and the reporting that landed on the big screen.
item.content:encoded: Follow on Apple or Spotify . Listen on the Reuters app. Reporter Jeff Horwitz is having a surreal week. His investigation into Facebook has been turned into a major Hollywood film starring Jeremy Allen White. On this episode of On Assignment , the Pulitzer Prize-winning Reuters journalist reflects on the Facebook Files investigation, his relationship with whistleblower Frances Haugen, and the impact the revelations had on the debate over social media's harms. He also shares what it's like to see his own story transformed for the big screen in Aaron Sorkin's The Social Reckoning . item.title: アップル、Ｍａｃのアクセス権限制御強化へ ＡＩリスク対策
item.description:
Stephen Nellis
[サンフランシスコ ２日 ロイター] - 米アップルは２日、同社のＰＣ「Ｍａｃ」の基本ソ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
アップル、Ｍａｃのアクセス権限制御強化へ　ＡＩリスク対策 13:57 配信

3月にニューヨーク市で開催されたアップルのイベント　REUTERS/Shannon Stapleton

Stephen Nellis

[サンフランシスコ ２日 ロイター] - 米アップルは２日、同社のＰＣ「Ｍａｃ」の基本ソフト（ＯＳ）を修正すると明らかにした。人工知能（ＡＩ）エージェントがＭａｃ内の全データへのアクセスを求めた場合に、利用者がより明確に認識し対応できるようにする。

メタ・プラットフォームズのＡＩエージェント「Ｍｕｓｅ」について、一部ユーザーから、機密性の高い個人情報にアクセスされたとの批判が出ている。

アップルのスマートフォン「ｉＰｈｏｎｅ」やタブレット端末「ｉＰａｄ」では、「サンドボックス化」と呼ばれる仕組みにより、初期設定ではどのアプリも別のアプリ内のデータにアクセスできない。一方、Ｍａｃはより柔軟な設計となっており、利用者の許可があれば、クラウドバックアップサービスなどのアプリが端末内の全データにアクセスできる「フルディスクアクセス」という設定がある。

アップルは２日、自社のサイトで、一部の開発者が利用者を危険にさらしかねない形でフルディスクアクセス機能を使っていると指摘し、今後、追加の制御機能を導入すると表明した。

「ＡＩエージェントの能力と自律性が高まるにつれ、これほど広範なアクセスに伴うリスクは大幅に増大する。利用者が自身のデータとプライバシーについて十分な情報に基づいて判断できるよう、アクセスを許可する前にこうしたリスクを明確に理解できるようにすることに取り組む」とした。

item.title: El Salvador pierde como local y queda cerca de descender en Liga de Naciones Concacaf
item.description: La selección de fútbol de El Salvador sufrió el viernes su segunda derrota consecutiva en la Liga de Naciones de la Concacaf al perder como local por 2-0 ante Jamaica con un doblete de Javon East, con lo que quedó en el último lugar del Grupo B de la Liga A y cerca de descender a la Liga B.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La selección de fútbol de El Salvador sufrió el viernes su segunda derrota consecutiva en la Liga de Naciones de la Concacaf al perder como local por 2-0 ante Jamaica con un doblete de Javon East, con lo que quedó en el último lugar del Grupo B de la Liga A y cerca de descender a la Liga B. Las selecciones que finalicen en quinto y sexto lugar de cada uno de los dos grupos de la Liga A descenderán a la Liga B. La "Selecta" ganó su primer partido de la competencia a Martinica por 3-1, pero posteriormente sufrió una goleada de 6-0 ante Guatemala, lo que la deja en el fondo del grupo por la diferencia negativa de goles. "No tengo palabras, es muy triste, algo que no esperábamos, quedamos a deber a nosotros mismos, al cuerpo técnico y a la afición. Así como ahorita estamos en el suelo nos vamos a levantar, vamos a salir adelante", dijo el defensa salvadoreño Jorge Cruz a la transmisión oficial de la Concacaf. El encuentro marcó el regreso de “La Selecta” -nombre coloquial del combinado centroamericano- al Estadio Cuscatlán de San Salvador, donde no jugaba desde el 14 de octubre de 2025, cuando perdió 0-1 ante Guatemala por las pasadas eliminatorias mundialistas. La selección dirigida por el colombiano Hernán Darío "Bolillo" Gómez, quien fue ratificado el miércoles, presentó cuatro cambios respecto a la goleada sufrida ante Guatemala. Al principio del encuentro, los salvadoreños parecieron mostrar una actitud más competitiva respecto a su anterior compromiso, producto del ingreso como titulares de Harold Osorio y Nathan Ordaz. Pero la situación se complicó a los 20 minutos cuando el zaguero Rudy Clavel vio la tarjeta roja tras una dura falta sobre el delantero Javon East, situación que aprovechó Jamaica para abrir el marcador a los 39 minutos cuando East se barrió en el área chica para empujar un centro enviado desde el sector izquierdo por Miguel Freckleton. En la parte complementaria, El Salvador mostró ímpetu, pero pocas ideas. Las dos opciones más claras de la selección local fueron generadas por jugadas individuales de Brayan Gil, que apenas inquietaron al portero jamaiquino Andre Blake. East marcó su doblete al minuto 64 cuando remató de zurda en el centro del área un pase de Jahmarie Nolan, quien estuvo cerca de anotar el tercero a los 67 con un peligroso remate de cabeza que desvió el guardameta. Los cerca de 9.500 aficionados que presenciaron una nueva derrota de El Salvador empezaron a abandonar el estadio antes de que finalizara el partido. El Salvador buscará su permanencia en la zona A el 5 de octubre cuando visite a Martinica en un partido que debe ganar y esperar una combinación de otros resultados. El presidente de la Federación Salvadoreña de Fútbol, Yamil Bukele, informó el miércoles que "Bolillo" Gómez renunciaría si se concreta el descenso a la Liga B. OTROS RESULTADOS En los otros partidos del grupo que se disputaron el viernes, Martinica remontó un gol en contra y venció por 2-1 a Honduras con tantos de Jonathan Varane y Jonathan Mexique a los 40 y 88 minutos, respectivamente. Erick Puerto había puesto en ventaja a los hondureños a los ocho minutos. En tanto, Surinam y Guatemala empataron sin goles. Con estos resultados, Surinam lidera el grupo con siete puntos, seguido por Jamaica con seis y Guatemala con cuatro. Más abajo se ubican Honduras, Martinica y El Salvador con tres unidades cada uno. En la última jornada del grupo que se disputará el 5 de octubre, Surinam visitará a Guatemala, mientras que Jamaica irá a Honduras. En el Grupo A, Costa Rica recompuso el jueves su camino al golear por 3-0 como visitante a Nicaragua en el partido que marcó el debut del ex jugador Bryan Ruiz como director técnico interino del representativo "tico" y el regreso del portero Keylor Navas. La Federación Costarricense de Fútbol (FCRF) nombró el lunes técnico interino a Ruiz, en sustitución del argentino Fernando Batista, quien fue despedido un día después de que la selección "tica" sufrió su segunda derrota consecutiva. En los otros partidos del jueves, Curazao ganó por 1-0 a Trinidad y Tobago, mientras que Haití goleó por 4-1 en su visita a República Dominicana. Curazao y Haití lideran el sector con nueve puntos cada uno, seguidos por República Dominicana con seis. Más abajo, se ubican Costa Rica con tres, además de Trinidad y Tobago y Nicaragua, que no han sumado. Los dos primeros lugares de cada uno de los dos grupos avanzarán a los cuartos de final, donde se unirán a las selecciones de México, Estados Unidos, Canadá y Panamá, que llegaron directamente a esa instancia por ser las mejores clasificadas de la Concacaf. Los ganadores de la fase de los cuartos de final clasificarán directamente a la Copa Oro del 2027. La Liga de Naciones es una competencia lanzada por la Concacaf en 2018 para garantizar que las 41 Asociaciones Miembro del organismo que rige el fútbol en Norteamérica, Centroamérica y El Caribe compitan regularmente en partidos oficiales entre las Copas del Mundo. Estados Unidos la ganó en 2021, 2023 y 2024. México logró el título en 2025.

item.title: Trump says US to send one-time $90 payment to 20 million seniors enrolled in Medicare
item.description: The payment to more than 20 million people is the latest promise the president has made to voters heading into the November midterms that will decide which party controls Congress.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump said the US government will send a one-time $90 payment to more than 20 million Americans enrolled in Medicare, a health insurance program for the elderly, to help offset the cost of their monthly medical insurance premiums. Trump said on social media late on Friday the payments will come from the Medicare Improvement Fund, which he said was given $2 billion by Congress to improve the Medicare fee-for-service program. The announcement is the latest in a series of financial promises the Republican leader has made to voters heading into the November midterm elections where control of Congress is at stake. Trump's Republican Party currently has a narrow majority in both the Senate and the House of Representatives but his approval rating [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"has been low"] over his handling of the high cost of living for Americans during the US-Israeli war on Iran that has spiked oil and gas prices. The White House released some details of Trump's plan on its website, saying most eligible seniors will receive the payment in the form of a direct deposit of $90 in early October. Those without direct deposit will receive a check, also sent in early October, to the mailing address they have registered with Medicare, the White House said. Last month, Trump proposed sending [USN:L6N45211D TEXT:"$5,000 checks"] to all adult citizens if the Republicans keep control of the House and Senate in the midterms, though analysts, economists and even some Republicans in Congress [USN:L6N452119 TEXT:"reacted with skepticism"] to the plan. The Trump administration is also separately sending [USN:L6N45K16K TEXT:"$500 payments"] to nearly 1 million Americans in a move that strategists say could potentially influence some election races. The White House says those payments were a refund for what it describes as excessive fees charged to people who purchased health insurance through the Affordable Care Act.

item.title: 米政権主要閣僚、イラン戦争やフーシ派巡り大統領山荘で協議 米報道
item.description: ［２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２日　ロイター］ - トランプ米政権の主要閣僚が２日、大統領山荘キャンプデービッドに集まり、イラン戦争、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派とサウジアラビアの紛争への対応を協議した。米ニュースサイトのアクシオスが複数の米当局者の話として伝えた。

アクシオスによると、会合はバンス副大統領が主宰し、ルビオ国務長官、ヘグセス国防長官、ウィットコフ大統領特使、ラトクリフ中央情報局（ＣＩＡ）長官、ケイン統合参謀本部議長らが参加した。トランプ政権はこの会合について公表していないが、当局者の１人は「物事が決定された、あるいは少なくとも掘り下げた議論が行われた」と述べたという。

トランプ氏は２日午後、記者団からイランに対する次の一手について問われ、「それを話せば、大ニュースになるだろう」と述べ、「いずれ分かる。非常にうまく進んでいる。イランは厳しい状況だ」と語った。

中東や欧米当局者はロイターに、サウジがフーシ派に対する攻勢を計画していると述べた。紅海の海上輸送路の確保に向け沿岸部で攻勢をかける案や、複数の戦線で同時攻撃を仕掛ける案などが検討されており、向こう数週間以内に開始する可能性があるという。

item.title: Joel Hofer, Blues start season with shutout win over Stars
item.description: Joel Hofer made 25 saves for his ninth career shutout and contributed an assist as the visiting St. Louis Blues beat the Dallas Stars 4-0 on Friday in the season opener for both teams.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Joel Hofer made 25 saves for his ninth career shutout and contributed an assist as the visiting St. Louis Blues beat the Dallas Stars 4-0 on Friday in the season opener for both teams. Pius Suter and Jimmy Snuggerud each had a goal and an assist and Mason McTavish and Dalibor Dvorsky also scored for the Blues. Stars goalie Jake Oettinger stopped 20 shots. It took McTavish just 1:34 into the game and the 2026-27 season to pick up his first goal as a Blue after being obtained from the Anaheim Ducks in an offseason trade. McTavish put in a loose puck from just outside the crease to give St. Louis a 1-0 lead. Hofer made a big save on Tyler Seguin's tip attempt on a Dallas power play in the final seconds of the opening period. St. Louis' Alexey Toropchenko was helped off the ice and left the game 3:28 into the second period after being sandwiched between two Dallas players along the boards behind the Blues' net. It appeared to be an arm or shoulder injury. Dvorsky made it 2-0 with 6:55 left in the second on only St. Louis' second shot of the period. Capitalizing on a Dallas turnover behind its own net, Dvorsky scored from the inside edge of the right circle after taking a pass from defenseman Philip Broberg. Oettinger fell after teammate Roope Hintz accidentally tripped the goalie as Oettinger tried to get back to the crease from behind the net. An apparent power-play goal by Blues defenseman Adam Jiricek, who was making his NHL debut, 1:06 into the third period was wiped out by Dallas' successful coach's challenge for offside. Hintz was helped off the ice 2:49 into the third period after a knee-on-knee hit by St. Louis defenseman Brandon Carlo, who was assessed a kneeing major and game misconduct. Hintz returned minutes later. Snuggerud and Suter picked up empty-net goals 15 seconds apart in the final 2:30. Hofer got an assist on Suter's goal. --Field Level Media

item.title: Shohei Ohtani set to hit in NLDS despite not being fully healthy
item.description: Shohei Ohtani admitted he won't be at full strength when he bats for the Dodgers in the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves, which begins Saturday in Los Angeles.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shohei Ohtani admitted he won't be at full strength when he bats for the Dodgers in the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves, which begins Saturday in Los Angeles. The four-time Most Valuable Player had a stint on the 15-day injured list in September due to right biceps and left knee issues that are still troubling him. He returned to go 5-for-21 (.238) with one extra-base hit, a double, and one RBI in the final five regular-season games. Speaking about his health, Ohtani said Friday through an interpreter, "I haven't been able to get a good grasp of the root cause of all this. I think that process is going to happen during the offseason when I'm going to have a little bit more time to be able to address it. But as of now, it's something I'm just going to have to manage." The two-way star previously was ruled out from any possible pitching work in the postseason -- and he hasn't taken the mound since July 3. "During the IL (stint), I pretty much knew I wasn't going to pitch the rest of the season," Ohtani said. "So I did focus on just the hitting aspect of the game and coming to understanding and wanting to execute and try new things when I came back. So, those were the things that I really took the IL time to think through what I wanted to try when I was back in action." Ohtani saw his offense fall off late in the season. In his final 18 games as the designated hitter, he went 11-for-70 (.157) with no homers and one RBI. Still, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said, "Shohei's not 100%, but he's going to be in the lineup. ... I think that most players that are performing now are not 100%. Obviously with Shohei, it's a bigger deal because of the player, but there's a lot of players that are not 100%, and they've just got to manage it. ... "I know that once the lights turn on, the postseason starts, the focus will be heightened. I expect good things. I really do. We just haven't seen it enough ... for me to forecast it." Overall on the season, Ohtani batted .275 with a .377 on-base percentage, a .512 slugging percentage, 30 homers and 81 RBIs in 139 games. In his abbreviated pitching campaign, he went 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, 95 strikeouts and 26 walks in 85 2/3 innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: US judge dismisses DOJ lawsuit that used abortion clinic access law against protesters
item.description: A US judge dismissed a lawsuit against pro-Palestinian organizations and protesters that President Donald Trump's administration brought last year under a law traditionally used against people blocking access to abortion clinics.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: A US judge dismissed a [USN:L6N3VG0UL TEXT:"lawsuit"] against pro-Palestinian organizations and protesters that President Donald Trump's administration brought last year under a law traditionally used against people blocking access to abortion clinics. US District Judge Katharine Hayden in New Jersey said the government's complaint did not adequately plead violations of the statute. She dismissed the claims without prejudice, saying the government can file an amended complaint within 30 days. The case was brought under the Freedom of Access to Clinic Entrances Act, or FACE Act, a 1994 law that prohibits the use of force and physical obstruction to interfere with people at reproductive health centers or houses of worship. In September 2025, the Justice Department sued pro-Palestinian activists that it accused of intimidating attendees during a November 2024 protest against an event at a synagogue in New Jersey. The event was billed by organizers as a spiritual service and real estate fair. It promoted the sale of property in Israeli settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. The lawsuit said the protest escalated into violence, alleging the demonstrators physically assaulted some worshippers and chanted and used vuvuzelas - plastic trumpets sometimes used by soccer fans - to disrupt the event. The Justice Department has brought several cases against protesters who have obstructed abortion clinics, but the case appeared to be the first time the law was used to allege interference with religious worship, according to Harmeet Dhillon, the head of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division. The Justice Department under Trump has curtailed the use of the FACE Act in abortion-related cases, alleging that past criminal prosecutions represented an improper politicized use of law enforcement. Dhillon said those restrictions do not apply to cases related to houses of worship. Last year, Trump pardoned several people prosecuted under the law. Trump has [USN:L4N3SN13Z TEXT:"attempted to deport"] foreign pro-Palestinian protesters, threatened [USN:FWN3TK1JE TEXT:"funding freezes"] for universities where protests were held, expanded [USN:L3N3QN23Z TEXT:"social media screening"] of immigrants and imposed [USN:S8N3S608Z TEXT:"sanctions on some of Israel's critics"]. His administration says pro-Palestinian protesters are antisemitic and support extremists. Demonstrators say their criticism of [USN:L4N44O22P TEXT:"Israeli attacks on Gaza"] and of Israel's occupation of Palestinian territories does not amount to antisemitism, and their advocacy for Palestinian rights should not be equated with supporting extremism.

item.title: Russia-Ukraine war is hitting India’s food and fertiliser security. Delhi has a role to play
item.description: The Black Sea region accounts for roughly a third of global wheat trade and 63% of the world’s sunflower oil exports. Food could be the next crisis for emerging economies.
item.dc:creator: Parthiva Bhaumik
item.content:encoded:
-->

Opinion

Russia-Ukraine war is hitting India’s food and fertiliser security. Delhi has a role to play

The Black Sea region accounts for roughly a third of global wheat trade and 63% of the world’s sunflower oil exports. Food could be the next crisis for emerging economies.

Parthiva Bhaumik

03 October, 2026 09:18 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Smoke rises from a civilian vessel on fire in the Black Sea off Odesa, Ukraine, on 19 July 2026 | Photo credit: Reuters/Stringer

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

F or much of the developing world, the defining shortage of the next two years may not be energy or credit. It may be food. Wheat prices are at a two-year high, fertiliser costs are climbing, and the shipping routes that carry staple grain to import-dependent countries are becoming harder to insure and use. Much of this traces to one stretch of water.

The Black Sea region accounts for roughly a third of global wheat trade and 63 per cent of the world’s sunflower oil exports . Its ports in Ukraine supply food products to more than 55 countries . India is among them, and among the most exposed. It is the world’s largest buyer of sunflower oil, and sources most of it from the Black Sea. It also depends on the same waters for important fertiliser supply lines.

India has spent the last few years arguing that the food and fertiliser security of developing countries cannot be left at the mercy of distant conflicts. It pressed the case through its G20 presidency and the Voice of the Global South summits and has been among the few large economies willing to speak for countries that import what they eat but control none of the routes their food travels on. For countries that buy their food in dollars and subsidise staples at home, a disruption thousands of miles away can very quickly become a problem for government budgets and household kitchens.

Show Full Article

The danger is no longer abstract for Indians either. In July, the Golden Leo , a cargo ship sailing from Ukraine, was struck by Russian cruise missiles off the Greater Odesa port. Nine of its seventeen crew members were killed, including four Indians . India already supplies more than 12 per cent of the global maritime workforce. With the government aiming for one in five seafarers worldwide to be Indian, attacks on commercial shipping put Indian maritime professionals disproportionately at risk.

This could hardly come at a worse time for India. Exporters are already being squeezed by US tariffs, while sanctions risk over Russian oil purchases and disruption at major energy chokepoints are pushing up costs across the economy. Food and fertiliser now threaten to become a third shock, arriving just as India is trying to absorb the first two.

Also Read: How Ukrainian assault on Russia’s largest Black Sea terminal threatens India’s crude imports

Food and fertiliser shocks hit India In India, the effects are already visible in cooking oil. Sunflower oil shipments from the Black Sea have been delayed by up to 60 days, and India’s imports have fallen 24 per cent this season to 2.48 million tonnes. Meanwhile, soybean oil purchases have risen 54 per cent as refiners look for alternatives.

Crude sunflower oil landed in India at around $1,496 a tonne in August, 18.4 per cent above the previous year. By comparison, palm oil prices rose 9.4 per cent and soybean oil 7.9 per cent.

Delhi has already cut import duties on edible oils, with the deepest reduction on sunflower oil, giving up revenue to limit the effect on consumers. Refiners are increasingly looking to Argentina , which has overtaken Ukraine as a supplier to India for the first time. But finding oil elsewhere is proving more expensive. Longer journeys add to costs just as more countries are competing for the same suppliers.

The second channel is fertiliser, and here the fiscal exposure is even larger. India relies heavily on imports from the Black Sea region and the Gulf, leaving it exposed to upheavals in both conflict zones. To avoid disruption in the Gulf, India has already rerouted procurement to Egypt, Algeria, Nigeria and Georgia. The Union Budget for 2026-27 allocated Rs 1.71 lakh crore for fertiliser subsidies, but the government may now need an additional Rs 70,000-80,000 crore as higher import costs push the bill well beyond budget. Subsidy spending on imported urea alone rose 128 per cent last year to nearly Rs 48,000 crore. A budget written on the assumption of easing global prices is being overtaken by the opposite.

Also Read: Ukraine’s robotic army is already at work. India must rethink the next battlefield

Delhi has leverage others don’t The wider problem is one India has spent the past decade warning about: countries across the Global South are forced to absorb shocks they did little to create. Bangladeshi buyers are now paying more than $450 a tonne for Australian wheat that cost under $380 before the disruption; replacing Black Sea supply can add another $25-60 a tonne. Somalia imports 90 per cent of its cereals, with six million people already facing acute hunger. These are the countries India has increasingly sought to speak for, and this time it is feeling the same pressure itself.

There is another reason for Delhi to become involved. India has consistently presented itself as a country willing to engage both sides in pursuit of peace, even when that position has attracted criticism.

An arrangement focused on protecting commercial food shipments would address an immediate problem shared by countries far beyond Europe while giving practical weight to its commitment to peace. It could start modestly with a food corridor between Indian and Black Sea ports, using Indian-flagged ships carrying grain, edible oil and fertiliser already bought by Indian buyers, with Indian maritime observers on board rather than military escorts. Striking an identifiable Indian ship carrying food to India or the Global South would carry a very different cost.

India also has leverage few others do. Its substantial economic relationship with Moscow gives Delhi a degree of access and economic weight that many countries simply do not have. It can use that position to press Moscow not to target civilian ships or the ports serving them, and to make the protection of commercial shipping part of the wider economic conversation between the two countries.

For India, this is no longer a distant war with distant consequences. Its seafarers are at risk, its food and fertiliser costs are rising, and the countries it has promised to speak for are being hit even harder. The Black Sea gives Delhi a rare chance to protect its own interests, stand up for the Global South and show what its commitment to peace can deliver in practice.

Parthiva Bhaumik is an analyst with the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change based in Kyiv. Views are personal.

item.title: JJ Peterka's overtime goal lifts Bruins past Jets
item.description: JJ Peterka scored with 1:39 left in overtime to propel the visiting Boston Bruins to a come-from-behind, 4-3 win over the Winnipeg Jets on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: JJ Peterka scored with 1:39 left in overtime to propel the visiting Boston Bruins to a come-from-behind, 4-3 win over the Winnipeg Jets on Friday night. David Pastrnak laid a pass ahead to Peterka as the duo surged in transition, and the Boston newcomer finished the deciding tally five-hole on Winnipeg's Stuart Skinner, who made 11 of his 26 stops in the third period and overtime. It was Peterka's second goal in as many games with Boston. Pastrnak assisted on Boston's final two goals. Elias Lindholm scored an extra-attacker goal with 1:38 left in regulation to force the game to the extra frame. Hampus Lindholm and James Hagens (first NHL goal) also scored while Jeremy Swayman made 30 saves for Boston, which has started the season with back-to-back wins. Kyle Connor had a power-play goal and added an assist, Mario Ferraro and Dylan DeMelo also lit the lamp, and Adam Lowry dished out a pair of helpers for the Jets in their season opener. After Skinner made several saves and got help from his right post on a Marat Khusnutdinov tip with 7:31 left in the third, the visitors' pressure paid off in a tying goal when Elias Lindholm was perfectly stationed between the circles to redirect a Pastrnak shot from above the right circle. Connor nearly ended the game in Winnipeg's favor 1:12 into the extra session, but he hit the left post after sliding through two defenders to attack the net. An opening goal at 4:52 highlighted Winnipeg's dominant start to the first. After Morgan Barron circled the zone and banked a pass off the boards, DeMelo blasted a point shot that changed direction and beat Swayman over his shoulder for a 1-0 lead. At the other end, Hampus Lindholm knotted the score with a point shot of his own at 9:23. Morgan Geekie picked up the puck along the wall and spun a feed to his defenseman for a blast that slipped past Skinner's glove. Hagens gave Boston its first lead with his milestone goal with 4:40 left before first intermission, cleaning up a loose puck in the crease after Mark Kastelic made a tough net drive. The Jets needed only 16 seconds of power-play time to make it 2-2 at 1:50 of the second. Cole Perfetti's turnaround shot led to a net-mouth scramble, with Connor corralling a loose puck at the right crease and sneaking it through traffic. Ferraro put Winnipeg back ahead in the middle frame with only eight seconds remaining, lasering a shot from the top of the left circle that appeared to clip Pastrnak on its way into the top corner. --Field Level Media

item.title: ＯＰＥＣプラスの生産能力評価、11月中旬にずれ込みか 中東紛争が影響
item.description:
Alex Lawler Olesya Astakhova
［ロンドン／モスクワ ２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Alex Lawler　Olesya Astakhova

［ロンドン／モスクワ　２日　ロイター］ - 石油輸出国機構（ＯＰＥＣ）加盟国とロシアなど非加盟産油国で構成する「ＯＰＥＣプラス」で、加盟国の２０２７年の原油生産枠（クオータ）設定に向けた生産能力の評価作業が遅れていることが関係者の話で分かった。イラン戦争で中東の増産計画が混乱し、生産予測が不透明になっているという。

生産能力評価は２０２６年９月末までに完了する予定だったが、関係者によると、１１月中旬になる見通し。

ＯＰＥＣプラス加盟国の生産能力の試算は米石油コンサルタント会社のデゴルヤー・アンド・マクノートンが行っている。米国の制裁下にあるロシア、イラン、ベネズエラは対象外。

関係筋によると、同社のＯＰＥＣへの報告書提出は１１月半ばになる。この日程でも、ＯＰＥＣプラスは１１月下旬に開く次回の全体会合で評価結果を検討できる。

中東紛争により、一部加盟国で生産能力の拡大を予定していた事業に遅れが生じている。関係筋は、名指しを控えつつ、評価に必要なデータを提出していない国もあると述べた。
